title: Getting started with PGS.TRI
text: required data input software simple: PGS values mothers, fathers, children needed. PGSxE interactions investigated, set environmental variables children required. Note environmental variables interactions need prepared. nature, model comparing within families environmental variables confounders corrected (need prepare data genetic principal components include model input, unless task look PGS x children’s PCs!). math, main effect environmental variables likelihood cancelled numerator denominator “automatically” corrects environmental variable disease model. can construct PGS trios using pre-trained weights available previously reported sources using external data, PGScatalog, following steps described unrelated individuals using softwares PLINK/2.0. Examples Autism Spectrum Disorders PGS000327, Orofacial Clefts PGS002266, Educational Attainment PGS002012 can obtained freely online.

title: Getting started with PGS.TRI
text: provide simple example running proposed method using simulated data. R function proposed method PGS-TRI. R function simulate data available simulation. also provide R function run polygenic TDT (pTDT) test pTDT (originally proposed Weiner et al, Nat Genet. 2017). PGSxE analysis, case-method also implemented case-(Allison et al, AJE 2019; Wang et al, AJE 2024). First simulate 200000 families based population disease risk model following logistic regression PGS main effect, two independent environmental variables \(E_1\) (binary) \(E_2\) (continuous), interaction effect PGS. Assume marginal disease prevalence Pr(D=1)=0.01. View simulated data. Randomly select 1000 affected probands families Fit proposed method randomly selected 1000 trios Print final results estimated direct PGS effect PGSxE interactions. “Estimate” refers log relative risk (log RR). original simulated data PGS main effect 0.4 interaction effect E. Print within-family variances average 1000 families. Print running time PGS.TRI() function 1000 trios.
code: #example analysis library(PGS.TRI) set.seed(04262023)  #Generate 200000 families with offsprings disease prevalence to be 1% dat = sim_prospective_population(n_fam=200000, #Number of families in the population                                cor_e_prs=FALSE, #Assuming no correlation between PGS and E                                cor_strat=0.25, #Random effect term to create population stratification bias in PGS                                rho2=0.25, #Random effect term to create population stratification bias in PGSxE                                alpha_fam=-5.5, #Intercept                                betaG_normPRS=0.4, #Main effect of PGS                                betaE_bin=0.2, #Main effect of E1                                betaE_norm=0.2, #Main effect of E2                                betaGE_normPRS_bin=0, #Interaction effect of PGSxE1                                betaGE_normPRS_norm=0, #Interaction effect of PGSxE2                                envir=TRUE) #Include environmental variables in the disease risk model ## Disease prevalence:  0.010645 head(dat$E_sim) ##      E_sim_bin E_sim_norm ## [1,]         1 -0.8068890 ## [2,]         1 -0.3576089 ## [3,]         1  0.3903469 ## [4,]         1 -0.5997115 ## [5,]         0 -0.2200456 ## [6,]         0 -0.6782173 head(dat$pgs_fam) ##           pgs_c      pgs_m      pgs_f ## [1,] -4.8184288 -3.5779866 -5.0108904 ## [2,]  0.2061615  0.4063380  0.6066281 ## [3,]  1.5035239  1.3617260  0.8225709 ## [4,] -0.1411008  0.1401712 -0.4475913 ## [5,] -0.6775838 -1.0829348 -0.2166373 ## [6,] -0.6639565 -0.3845802 -0.7305453 table(dat$D_sim) ##  ##      0      1  ## 197871   2129 id = sample(which(dat$D_sim==1),size=1000,replace=F) PRS_fam = dat$pgs_fam[id,] envir = dat$E_sim[id,] startTime <- Sys.time() res_sim = PGS.TRI(pgs_offspring = PRS_fam[,1],                   pgs_mother = PRS_fam[,2],                   pgs_father = PRS_fam[,3],                  GxE_int = TRUE, #If GxE_int is FALSE, then fit a model without interaction effect between PGSxE. "formula" and "E" will be ignored in the function.                  formula = ~ factor(E_sim_bin)+E_sim_norm, #For categorical variables, remember to add factor().                  E = envir,                  parental_indirect = FALSE, #If indirect polygenic effect from parents are considered, set this to TRUE.                  side = 2) ## The complete number of trios with non-missing environmental variables is 1000 endTime <- Sys.time() res_sim$Coefficients_direct ##                             Estimate  Std.Error    Z.value       Pvalue ## PGS                       0.38144038 0.11200084  3.4056920 0.0006599659 ## PGS x factor(E_sim_bin)1 -0.09540744 0.14213861 -0.6712282 0.5020751927 ## PGS x E_sim_norm          0.06266046 0.06584785  0.9515947 0.3413025606 head(res_sim$var_fam) ## [1] 0.1145986 0.5482620 0.0384810 0.7079308 0.9436784 0.4002518 length(res_sim$var_fam) ## [1] 1000 sum(res_sim$var_fam)/length(res_sim$var_fam) ## [1] 0.4369649 print(endTime - startTime) ## Time difference of 0.1461999 secs

title: PGS.TRI — PGS.TRI
text: pgs_offspring PGS values affected probands (children). vector length N, missing values allowed pgs_mother PGS values mothers corresponds children. vector length N, missing values allowed pgs_father PGS values fathers corresponds children. vector length N, missing values allowed GxE_int Whether interaction effect pgs environmental variables interest model. FALSE, "formula" "E" ignored. parental_indirect Whether estimate potential parental indirent effect, returns estimated difference mother father parental effect (delta_MF = beta_M - beta_F). formula environmental variables interest PGSxE interaction effect E environmental variables interest interaction effect. vector length N one environmental variable data frame/data matrix NxP P environmental variables allowed. side Sided Wald test, default 2-sided. smalltriosize Whether number trios small (<100), TRUE, t test used rather wald test.

title: PGS.TRI — PGS.TRI
text: list results PGS.TRI Coefficients_direct Results direct PGS effect, GxE_int TRUE, result also include PGSxE interaction effects Coefficients_indirect Results indirect parental PGS effect difference: PGS_mother - PGS_father var_fam Within-family variances family var_fam_sum Sum within-family variances log_LC Log likelihood offspring's transmission component log_LP_profile log profile likelihood parents' component, note can report likelihood considering direct effects model log_likelihood Results final log-likelihood. calculated sum offspring's parents' components vcov Variance-covariance matrix coefficients direct genetic effects gene–environment interaction terms (PGS×E)
